title: NRM common definitions
description: Shared definitions for NVIS Resource Model v0.1. Referenced by every entity schema in this directory. Nothing here is an entity; there is no top-level object to validate against this file.

uuid.description: An opaque surrogate key. Mint a UUIDv7 for new records: it is time-ordered, so it indexes and sorts usefully, and it is still opaque. Any RFC 9562 UUID validates, because records imported from a system that already minted a v4 must not be forced to change identity.

identifier_format.description: How to read the accompanying value. The first ten members are Redfish's DurableNameFormat verbatim, so a Redfish payload crosswalks without translation. The last four are NVIS extensions for identity Redfish has no format for.

oneOf.title: InfiniBand GUID (NVIS extension)
oneOf.description: Node, port or system GUID as reported by ibnetdiscover or UFM. Redfish has no InfiniBand identity format, and this is the join key for every fabric validation we run.

oneOf.title: GPU UUID (NVIS extension)
oneOf.description: The GPU-xxxxxxxx form reported by nvidia-smi and used as the DCGM label. Distinct from the UUID format because the GPU- prefix is part of the value everywhere it appears, and stripping it would break every existing join.

oneOf.title: NVLink GUID (NVIS extension)
oneOf.description: NVLink endpoint or switch identity, needed to distinguish a logical NVLink from the physical cable cartridge carrying it.

oneOf.title: Manufacturer serial number (NVIS extension)
oneOf.description: The serial as printed and as it appears on the packing list. Scoped by the manufacturer of the resource's type, because serials are not globally unique.

identifier.description: One way the physical world names this resource. A resource carries as many as are known, and reconciliation matches on any of them. This is what lets a surrogate primary key coexist with real-world identity: nothing is forced to choose one true name.

value.description: Verbatim as the source system reports it. Do not normalize case, strip prefixes, or reformat separators: the value's job is to match, and every normalization is a chance to stop matching.

scope.description: Namespace within which the value is unique, where it is not globally unique. Required in practice for SERIAL (use the manufacturer) and useful for site-scoped names.

source.description: System this identifier was read from, for example nautobot, ufm, redfish, dcgm, packing-list.

observation.description: Whether this record states design intent or a measurement. First-class on every entity and every relation, because the difference between the two IS the validation product: a cabling file says expected, ibnetdiscover says observed, and the diff is the defect list. No surveyed standard carries this distinction, which is why it is here rather than crosswalked.

lifecycle.description: Where the resource is in its life, not whether it is healthy right now. Health is telemetry and belongs in DCGM or Prometheus; putting it here would invite a slow inventory database to be polled as a monitoring system.

part_location.description: Redfish PartLocation, for addressing something inside something else. This is how a transceiver in a cage in a tray gets an address without inventing a path syntax.

service_label.description: The label as silkscreened on the hardware, which is what an operator standing at the rack can actually read.

location_ordinal_value.description: Zero-based index within the parent, per Redfish.

external_refs.description: Foreign keys into systems that are authoritative for something. Nautobot is the asset source of record per the InfoSec Asset Management Standard, and its resource_id custom field exists expressly to hold the other direction of this join -- so `nautobot` here plus `resource_id` there is a bidirectional link, not a copy. NRM does not compete with these systems; it references them.

propertyNames.description: Lowercase system name: nautobot, ufm, redfish, bcm, dcgm, servicenow.

labels.description: Free-form key/value tags for local use. Deliberately outside the modelled fields: a team needs somewhere to put something the contract does not cover, and without this they would either abuse a modelled field or refuse the contract. Nothing normative may depend on a label.

provenance.description: Where this record came from. Required in practice for anything imported, because a validation failure whose first question is 'which file said this?' costs an afternoon to answer otherwise.

source.description: System or file kind: nautobot, ufm, rack-inventory-xlsx, p2p-cabling-csv, bcm-netautogen, dcgm, manual.

source_ref.description: Locator within the source: a filename, a URL, a row number, a Nautobot object ID.

collected_at.description: When the source produced this, not when NRM ingested it. An observed record whose collected_at is three weeks old is not evidence about today.

collected_by.description: Tool and version, or a person. `ibnetdiscover 3.2.1` is useful; `script` is not.

first_seen.description: First observation. Together with last_seen this answers 'has this been missing since the maintenance window?', which is the question asked during every bring-up.
